description: GLOBAL Renovate policy (RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE in .github/workflows/renovate.yaml) — the supply-chain baseline AND the shared classification enforced on EVERY repo the homelab-renovate App autodiscovers. This is the platform's Renovate policy; a repo needs NO renovate.json to be correctly classified (onboarding:false + requireConfig:optional). A per-repo renovate.json is only for genuine overrides. Implements the S2C2F (consumer) leg of docs/slsa.md; the agentic lanes: docs/renovate.md + docs/agents/merge-path.md (FU-046 open). dependencyDashboard is OFF by operator ruling (2026-08-18): the dashboard is an interactive click-ops surface whose approval/rebase checkboxes nothing here uses — every lane keys on labels; Renovate liveness is the exporter-gauge signal (FU-125), never dashboard-issue-exists.

force.description: Force-wins over PRESETS resolved at REPO level (renovate merge order: the global file's `extends` is moved into the repo config, resolved there, and merged ON TOP of the global keys — so `config:recommended` → `:dependencyDashboard` → true beat the `dependencyDashboard: false` above on EVERY repo; 10 dashboards open 2026-09-27, agent-coordinator#24 reopened within one run of being closed even with no Repository Problems and no pending branches — debug dry-run, renovate 44.115.12, dependency-dashboard.js:205 gates on this value alone). With the gate false Renovate runs ensureIssueClosing on the next run: the dashboards close themselves. `:dependencyDashboard` in sleep-tracking / sleep-iac / oracle-iac renovate.json is overridden too (delete those lines for hygiene).

argocd.description: Class 1 — Helm charts, GitOps (docs/dependency-upgrades.md §The dependency inventory; S9 #1985 next step 7, 2026-10-04). The `argocd` manager has NO default file match, so until this block every chart bump in argocd/platform/*.yaml was hand-proposed (homelab#2200, found by an FU sweep). The pattern is the Application files only — `argocd/platform/values/` holds `$values` files, not pins. OCI charts (ghcr.io/… repoURLs) resolve through the docker datasource, so the docker timestamp-optional rule below covers their cooldown. `prHourlyLimit: 3` (root, above — the limits are root-only, never a packageRule; was TEMPORARILY 6 from 2026-10-04 to drain the first class-1/2 wave under watch, back to 3 on 2026-10-05 once the ~30-bump backlog was through) paces a wave: with the 6-hourly run that is ≤3 new PRs per run per repo, so a backlog drains over days instead of landing as one wave on the reviewer and the shared App GraphQL pool (FU-290 — the 2026-09-25 wave drained it). `prConcurrentLimit` stays at the default 10: a lower ceiling is eaten by PRs parked on a human (`major/awaiting-human`, a red sentinel) and would stall the drain.

kubernetes.description: Class 2 — in-cluster images, GitOps: the `kubernetes` manager over the per-service manifests ArgoCD syncs (third-party `image:` refs; the first-party ghcr.io/teststuffstash/** refs are class 3 and excluded by the rule below). `agents/coordinator/*.yaml` is deliberately NOT in the pattern: `/agents/` is codeowner-gated, so a Renovate PR there parks on the human the lane exists to remove — those refs stay on the deploy-pin sweep / hand bumps until that gate moves.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes are the exception to the cooldown — get them in fast (CI still gates). `automerge` label → the renovate-approve reflex approves; auto-merged so exposure is minimal. A security fix that is ALSO a major keeps the `major` label from the catch-all rule (this block cannot filter by update type): the reflex refuses `major` and the un-armed major rides the coordinator's lane — the cooldown exception still applies.

packageRules.description: Digest / pin bumps (any manager) — a human can't review a hash → mechanical `automerge` lane (org cooldown + CI gate + renovate-approve reflex).

GitHub Actions — EVERY update type, majors included (operator 2026-09-27: an Actions major is not a 'major major' until evidence says so; no lens review has yet found an upstream change that mattered — #14, allure#18-#21 all N/A). The mechanical lane IS the evidence collector: CI on the bumped head + the FU-1990 revert chain. A dependency GRADUATES to the ungrouped, lens-reviewed `major` lane (the rule after the major catch-all) the first time it produces evidence — a merged revert-wf-* PR naming it, a red major PR, or a review asking for an in-PR adaptation / filing a follow-up — one line in that rule's matchPackageNames, operator-direct. SHA-pinned org-wide (pinGitHubActionDigests already defeats tag-repointing) → mechanical automerge. ONE PR PER REPO PER WAVE (groupName): Renovate works in batches, and a batch reviewed as N single-dependency PRs is N reviewer rides that each see one member and N updater/CI rounds as each merge puts the rest BEHIND (agent-coordinator#14–#18, 2026-09-26). rebaseWhen behind-base-branch: Renovate keeps its OWN branch current and RE-EXTRACTS master on every rebase (a call site added on master after the PR opened gets bumped — the #14 third-call-site defect), which the org default `conflicted` cannot do and the docs call wrong for automerge + strict checks; a branch someone else pushed to stays untouched (Renovate's edited-PR rule), so the in-cluster updater (agents/update-pr-branch.sh) leaves untouched Renovate PRs to Renovate.
pre-commit hooks patch/minor — mechanical automerge.
Python DEV deps (pytest/ruff/…) patch/minor — mechanical automerge. poetry added 2026-07-16 (allure-behavior-snippets): same dep class, same lane, regardless of package manager.

Python RUNTIME deps (boto3/…) patch/minor — meaningful (runs in prod, changelogs exist) → the LLM `deps-review` lane: armed, reviewed by the merge-path review reflex, worker adapts on CHANGES_REQUESTED (FU-046). poetry added 2026-07-16.

Pins and digests: the cooldown is TIMESTAMP-OPTIONAL. A pin (tag → SHA) or a digest move changes nothing semantically, and the releases it references often carry no timestamp (homelab#2021, 2026-09-27: `renovate/stability-days` PENDING forever on the grouped Actions pin PR — the same class as the Docker finding below). Without this the first pin PR of every repo can never merge.

Docker datasource: the 7-day cooldown is TIMESTAMP-OPTIONAL. Docker tags carry no release timestamp, and under the default timestamp-required behaviour every base-image release is marked pending FOREVER (agent-coordinator debug dry-run 2026-09-27: 'Marking 29 release(s) as pending, as they do not have a releaseTimestamp' — node 22→24 could never be proposed), which also force-enables the Dependency Dashboard Renovate keeps reopening on that repo (a pending internalChecksFilter branch makes Renovate ensure the dashboard regardless of dependencyDashboard: false). Trade-off accepted: no cooldown on base images — CI (the image build) and the deploy-pin revert are the gate.

npm packages via the `deno` manager — homelab's only JS surface is scripts/mermaid-lint (deno.json imports + deno.lock: mermaid + linkedom, the docs' mermaid parser; ADR-143 retired its package.json/npm lane 2026-09-29). CI-only dev tooling exercised by required `ci` on every PR (the parse, run with NO Deno permissions). `lock-intake-lint` (ADR-143, a `ci` step) fails any lockfile change bringing in an OSV-flagged, <7-day-old or install-script package version — transitive ones included, which Renovate's osvVulnerabilityAlerts (direct deps only) and minimumReleaseAge (the bumped dep only) never see. Renovate's `deno install --frozen=false` honours deno.json's minimumDependencyAge, so the regenerated lock is floored too. Patch/minor → mechanical automerge; majors → the catch-all. `npm` stays in the list for stack repos that still carry a package.json.

Terraform providers (lockfile + version constraints) — the MANAGEMENT BOX is the gate, mechanically (ADR-131 amended 2026-09-27, homelab#2026, S9 #1988): stage 1 of the sentinel admits the `provider-pin` diff shape (only version / constraints / hash lines, every provider source unchanged), stage 2 plans the head with the new provider (registry-signed, hash-verified by tofu) and a pin head must plan EMPTY — `management-sentinel` is green on +0 ~0 -0 and red (`provider bump changes the plan: <root>(…) — human read`) otherwise. With ci + the sentinels green the renovate-approve reflex approves and auto-merge lands it; the red ones are the only provider PRs a human sees. Six such PRs (2026-09-25..27) all planned +0 under human orders — the human added nothing (operator: 'I don't want to see these PRs for years to come'). Roots the box does NOT plan (policy foreign_roots) are excluded by the rule after this one rather than merged unplanned (#1984 merged that way, reconciled from the jail after the fact). NON-MAJOR ONLY (2026-09-28, homelab#2037/#2046/#2047): without a matchUpdateTypes restriction this rule's `addLabels` leaked `automerge` onto terraform MAJORS — the major catch-all below flips automerge to false but addLabels MERGE and nothing removes a label — so a major was born un-armed AND wearing the mechanical lane's marker; the renovate-approve reflex rubber-stamped it as the reviewer's own identity and the migration lens refused on own-verdict-at-head forever. Majors here take the catch-all (un-armed, `major`, the coordinator's lane); the reflex additionally refuses any `major`-labelled PR and the scan strips a leaked label (coordinator-scan.sh stale-stamp repair).

Terraform roots the management box does not plan (policy/mgmt/plan-input.yaml foreign_roots: tofu/infisical port-forwards into the live cluster; tofu/cloudflare-token is the one-shot admin-token root) — no sentinel plan exists for them, so a provider bump there has no gate. Disabled: their providers move by hand with a jail plan (docs/management-box.md §MB3), and tofu/infisical is slated to leave tofu (docs/dependency-upgrades.md).
Dockerfile base-image VERSION minor (e.g. python 3.11→3.12) — behavior change → `deps-review`.

Regex-managed pins (the customManagers below: devbox/nix in the arc-runner image, s5cmd in the coordinator image) patch/minor — a pinned download the image build exercises in `ci` (push: false), so CI is the gate → mechanical automerge; the cluster image pin is the revert. Until 2026-09-27 these bumps had NO lane (an un-armed `dependencies` PR nobody owned — the #1988 unlabelled class). Majors → the catch-all (human lane). The two VERSION-SET partners (crossplane engine digest, cloudflared in tofu/cloudflare) are excluded so their grouped PRs ride the argocd/kubernetes lane's labels. Operator ruling the same day: pin only what Renovate updates — a pin Renovate cannot bump is worse than a weekly float.

Devbox/Nix tools — DISABLED everywhere: the `@latest` pins have no trackable version, so Renovate mis-resolves them (downgrades gitleaks to a dead 5-yr-old release — sleep-tracking#15). Devbox updates ride the weekly synchronized `devbox-update.yaml` instead (docs/renovate.md).

First-party reusable workflows (`uses: teststuffstash/<repo>/.github/workflows/…@master`) are NOT Renovate's — the floating @master IS the contract: a fix in homelab reaches every caller at once. pinGitHubActionDigests froze every caller at one homelab commit and would then open a digest PR per homelab master move (2026-09-25, oracle-fleet#737). Same rule as first-party images (docs/dependency-upgrades.md class 3): our own artifacts never ride Renovate.

First-party IMAGES and CHARTS (ghcr.io/teststuffstash/**) are NOT Renovate's — class 3 (docs/dependency-upgrades.md): the image repo's deploy-pin PR moves them (ADR-084) and a `2026.<m>.<d>-g<sha>` tag does not order. Same rule as the first-party Actions one above. Datasource-scoped (not manager-scoped) so it holds wherever such a ref appears — the `kubernetes` manager's manifests, the `argocd` manager's openrouter-operator OCI chart (ghcr.io/teststuffstash/charts), a tofu Deployment image.

ARC controller + runner scale sets move in LOCKSTEP (class 1's canary cell: three Applications, one chart version — arc-controller, arc-runners, arc-runners-large). One grouped PR so a merge never leaves the controller and the runners on different chart versions.

Crossplane is a VERSION SET (docs/dependency-upgrades.md §Version SETS): the chart pin in argocd/platform/crossplane.yaml AND the `crossplane.io/engine-image-digest.<version>` annotation next to it, which publicroute-tf-validate keys by chart version to render the composition with the engine pulled BY DIGEST (homelab#1779). A chart bump alone is CI-red forever — #2224 (2.3.2 → 2.3.6, 2026-10-04) was the first Renovate crossplane PR and proved it. The regex customManager below moves the annotation (version in the KEY, digest in the VALUE — crossplane's chart version equals its engine tag v<version>); this group puts both in ONE PR. Labels come from the argocd rule only (the custom.regex automerge rule excludes this dep) so the grouped PR rides `deps-review`, never the mechanical lane.

cloudflared is a VERSION SET (docs/dependency-upgrades.md §Version SETS): the connector image in argocd/resources/publicroute/composition.yaml (`kubernetes` manager) AND `cloudflared_image` in tofu/cloudflare/variables.tf (the regex customManager below) — the repo's own comment declares them the same pin, and Renovate's first cloudflared PR (#2232, 2026.5.2 → 2026.9.3, 2026-10-04) moved the composition's half alone; the reviewer's version-set finding (G13). One group, one PR; labels come from the kubernetes rule (`deps-review`), the custom.regex automerge rule excludes this dep. The seat applies tofu/cloudflare after the merge (docs/runbook.md §Cloudflare).

Class 1/2 (charts in argocd/platform, images in argocd/resources) patch/minor → the LLM `deps-review` lane (FU-046): armed, the merge-path review reflex reviews, APPROVED merges, ArgoCD auto-sync is the deploy edge. Not `automerge`: a chart minor re-renders manifests and an image minor runs in prod — there is something to read. Digest bumps take the mechanical rule at the top; majors take the catch-all below (un-armed, `major` — the CRD-carrying charts Argo/Crossplane/cert-manager/ESO/CNPG reach the human lane by update type, IAC-G09).

EVERY major bump (all repos, all managers) carries `major` — the MIGRATION LENS marker (semver decides whether the lens runs: the reviewer does upstream research + known issues + platform compatibility before any verdict). The LANE is decided by BLAST CLASS (S9 homelab#1985, 2026-09-25): by default a major is NOT armed = the HUMAN-GATED coordinator lane (investigate while red, worker adapts if in-budget, agents/major-handoff.sh → a human merges — docs/agents/merge-path.md §Reflexes vs judgment; un-armed = invisible to the review reflex, coordinator-scan owns it). GitHub Actions are excluded (`!github-actions`): they ride the grouped mechanical lane above until a dependency graduates into the rule after this one. Order matters: the last matching rule's automerge wins, addLabels merge.

GRADUATED GitHub Actions majors — the 'major majors' (operator 2026-09-27): dependencies whose Actions major has produced evidence that a human should care (a merged revert-wf-* PR naming it, a red major PR, a review asking for an in-PR adaptation or filing a follow-up). UNGROUPED (one PR per dependency: precise revert, precise reverted-pin refusal, one lens ride), `major`-labelled, ARMED but NOT `automerge`-labelled: the review reflex reviews armed non-automerge PRs, so the migration lens (agents/lenses/migration.md) is the merge gate and a post-merge push-only failure still rolls back via FU-1990. Add a dependency here with ONE line in matchPackageNames when it bites; the list starts empty (the placeholder name matches nothing — the drill's deliberate downgrade of actions/create-github-app-token is not evidence). ADR-141 amended 2026-09-27.

Deployment IMAGE tags in tofu — the docker datasource under the terraform manager (`image = "<ref>"` on a kubernetes_deployment) — are ARMED at every update type (ADR-141 amended 2026-09-28, #1988's class row; drilled the same day): non-majors already ride the terraform `automerge` rule above; a MAJOR keeps `major` from the catch-all (this rule only arms it, no `automerge` label) so the migration lens reviews it and its APPROVED completes the merge — the Actions pattern. The management box applies the merge (kubernetes_deployment.* is allowlisted), the tofu-image-revert chain (agents/coordinator/deploy-revert-argo.yaml) reverts a stuck rollout, and scripts/pin-only-lint.sh check (f) refuses the re-proposal for 30 days. Precondition per Deployment: the ADR-140 shape (2 replicas, zero-unavailable rollout, PDB) — an RWO singleton never enters this lane, which is why the rule is scoped by datasource, not by file. `behind-base-branch` so an armed major that fell behind master is rebased by Renovate, not left to a human.

Terraform PROVIDER majors — ARMED (operator 2026-10-04, S9 #1988; ADR-131 as amended 2026-10-04). Same shape as the Deployment-image rule above: the major keeps `major` from the catch-all and gets NO `automerge` label, so the renovate-approve reflex refuses it and the migration lens (agents/lenses/migration.md) is the merge gate — its APPROVED completes the merge. What stands behind that merge, all built and drilled before this rule: the box sentinel's provider-pin gate (a pin head must plan EMPTY relative to master's own pending plan, or be a default backfill, and may not raise any stored schema/identity version — PR#2205), the empty plan IS the deploy, `MgmtApplyErroredOnNewProvider` names the provider when its first CHANGING apply errors (PR#2206), and the `tofu-provider-revert` chain reverts the introducing pin on that alert (PR#2207; drilled 2026-10-04, #2209: alert → merged + applied revert, no human). A major whose plan is not empty or whose plan ERRORS (helm 3, #2046: the `kubernetes {}` block) is red on the sentinel and never auto-merges — the worker adapts in-PR and the adaptation is no longer a pin-only diff. The two humans this lane still has: a red sentinel (`mgmt-human-plan`) and a lens that requests changes. The residual accepted here is the same as for Actions and Deployment images: a change that plans empty, applies clean and is still wrong later — the lens's upstream read is the only defence. First real acceptance: the first `MgmtApplyErroredOnNewProvider` firing on a real apply (the detector is fixture- and drill-proven only). `behind-base-branch` so an armed major that fell behind master is rebased by Renovate, not left to a human.

argo-workflows chart MAJORS — ARMED (operator 2026-10-05, ADR-149; the chain was drilled the same day: #2276 bump → synthetic ArgoControllerSilent → #2279 revert merged + synced in 10 min, no human). Same shape as the provider-major rule above: the major keeps `major` from the catch-all and gets NO `automerge` label, so the renovate-approve reflex refuses it and the migration lens (agents/lenses/migration.md) is the merge gate — its APPROVED completes the merge. The lens READS APPVERSION FROM THE CHART INDEX: chart semver is not app semver (1.0.24→1.1.1 was the app major 4.0→4.1 and rode deps-review unlensed, #2238; #2254, two lens rounds, was packaging). Behind the merge: ArgoControllerSilent (triage now, fails closed) is the post-deploy verdict; the chart-revert webhook receiver (argocd/resources/chart-revert/, OUTSIDE Argo Workflows' cone) reverts the pin-only merge as revert-chart-<sha8> with a `reverted-charts:` line; scripts/pin-only-lint.sh check (h) refuses the re-proposal for 30 days. Scoped to ONE chart — a second chart joins only on its own evidence (a drilled chain for the thing it breaks). `behind-base-branch` so an armed major that fell behind master is rebased by Renovate, not left to a human.

customManagers.description: Crossplane engine image digest annotation in argocd/platform/crossplane.yaml — the chart's VERSION SET partner (the `crossplane` group rule above). publicroute-tf-validate reads `crossplane.io/engine-image-digest.<chart targetRevision>` and pulls the engine by that digest; a bump with no matching key fails the gate (homelab#1779). The engine image TAG (v<chart version>) lives in the annotation KEY and the digest in its VALUE — both captured, both rewritten; the gate derives the same key from the chart pin. The key carries the TAG, not the bare version: with extractVersionTemplate stripping the v, Renovate looked the digest up for tag `2.3.6` and dropped the update ("Could not determine new digest", #2228 shipped the chart alone). If Renovate ever wrote a wrong digest the gate's digest pull fails and the PR is red — never a bad merge. By hand: `crane digest docker.io/crossplane/crossplane:v<targetRevision>`.

arc-runner image toolchain ARGs (FU-015 residual): DEVBOX_VERSION / NIX_VERSION in docker/arc-runner/Dockerfile — pinned binaries outside any stock manager. github-releases datasource; patch/minor ride the normal lanes, majors hit the human gate like everything else.

s5cmd in the agent-coordinator image (coordinator/Dockerfile, the transcript-capture uploader): the release-asset URL carries the version twice (path + asset name) — one regex, both captures must agree. github-releases datasource; patch/minor ride the custom.regex lane, majors the human lane. Pinned BECAUSE Renovate updates it (operator 2026-09-27); claude-code and gh in the same image float to latest on the weekly rebuild by design.

cloudflared in tofu/cloudflare/variables.tf — the composition's VERSION SET partner (the `cloudflared` group rule above). The one-off connector's Deployment reads `var.cloudflared_image`, so the terraform manager's kubernetes_deployment image extraction never sees the ref — it lives in a variable DEFAULT, not an `image = "…"` literal (git log: Renovate never touched this file). Tag and digest both captured and rewritten, the same docker datasource as the composition's pin so both classify alike and group.
